title: Uptime Command Center: Activation Slate & Cross-Functional Sprint Plan
body:
Purpose: Stand up an "Uptime Command Center" (UCC) — a lightweight, cross-functional activation slate to reduce time-to-detect and time-to-recover for platform-wide SLO degradations. This doc is a tactical 60-day sprint plan + onboarding checklist intended for the first pilots and for stakeholder alignment.

Context and why now:
- We keep seeing multi-service latency spikes where detection-to-first-action is 20–40 minutes. Some of that is tooling gaps, some is unclear roles.
- Objective: compress mean time to mitigation for critical SLO breaches to <10 minutes for P1 (customer-facing generation latency) and <30 minutes for P2 (batch embedding throughput), by improving signal routing, decision authority, and playbook discoverability.

What the UCC is (quick):
- A temporary, staffed coordination hub for SLO incidents and large-scale degradations. Think: war-room-lite for incidents that affect multi-product teams or cross-region model fallbacks.
- Not a permanent org; a process and rotation for 60–90 day pilots, with clear handoffs back to feature teams.

Scope for pilot (60 days):
- Services: hosted-api gateway, request-router, cache layer, and model-serving tier.
- Signals: latency 95/99, error-rate for generation endpoints, tail-queue time, model-fallback count, cost spike alerts tied to autoscaling.
- Stakeholders: eng-sre (lead), serving-runtime, platform-engineering, product-hosted-api, customer-success (for customer impact triage).

Success metrics (relative, measurable):
- Detection-to-first-action median <= 10 minutes for P1 incidents.
- Mean customer-facing outage time reduced by 30% across pilot services.
- 80% of on-call teams report runbooks are discoverable within 3 minutes under stress test.

Command structure and roles (initial):
- UCC Lead (rotation): responsible for convening stakeholders, declaring scope, and authorizing mitigations. Owner: Aisha Malik (pilot lead).
- Incident Navigator: zooms on signal triage and routes logs/traces; Owner: Ben Thompson.
- Model/Runtime Liaison: responsible for model fallbacks and quantization variant routing; Owner: Ravi Kapoor.
- Customer Impact Liaison: surfaces high-touch customers and coordinates comms with CS; Owner: Mariana Lopez.
- Artifact Scribe: documents decisions and action items in real time (Confluence + postmortem stub); Owner: Evan Cho.

Playbook index (to create and validate during sprint):
1) Latency tail spike (95th vs 99th divergence) — detection rules, initial checks (cache hit ratio, KV cache misuse), quick mitigations (pin old model, tighten batching), rollback criteria.
2) Model fallback storm — criteria for automatic fallback vs manual override, traffic split thresholds, telemetry to confirm recovery.
3) Burst autoscale cost shock — soft-cap policy, temporary throttles, billing alert disablement guardrails.
4) Cross-region network blip — fallback routing, warm standby checks, client-retry guidance.

Operational experiments (week-by-week plan):
- Week 0 (prep, 1 week): validate alert definitions, make test channel in Slack, create Confluence UCC index with quick-link cards per playbook. Run tabletop with 6 participants.
- Week 1–2 (initial run, 2 weeks): run daily 30-min UCC standups at 9:00am PT; simulate a latency tail incident (synthetic). Capture timelines.
- Week 3–4 (process tweak, 2 weeks): adjust detection thresholds to reduce noise (goal FPR down 25%), add pre-authorized mitigations for model pinning.
- Week 5–6 (scale test, 2 weeks): introduce multi-service scenario (gateway + model store + cache). Evaluate handoff friction and instrumentation gaps.
- Week 7–8 (handoff & retro, 2 weeks): transition operations back to service owners with a 30-day watch; run retro and publish lessons.

Sprint backlog (candidate tickets):
- Create UCC Slack shortcuts and alert routing: JIRA-OPS-5210 (owner: Ben).
- Confluence: UCC index + playbook stub pages for four incidents: CONFL-122 (owner: Evan).
- Instrumentation: add model-fallback counter and sample percentiles for KV cache: GH-serve-988 (owner: Ravi).
- Telemetry: add 'first-action' marker to SLO incident spans and surface in dashboards: MET-308 (owner: Platform SRE).
- Runbook audit: surface missing runbooks and mark owners (internal doc task): DOC-41 (owner: Product SRE).

Communication plan (internal + external):
- Internal: #ops-command-center channel as primary. UCC lead posts a 1-paragraph status update every 30 minutes during active incidents; Artifact Scribe posts final timeline in Confluence within 2 hours of mitigation.
- External (customer-facing): CS drafts templated notifications for common incident types during pilot; legal/comms loop included for any customer-impacting >30m.

Onboarding checklist for a UCC shift (short checklist):
- Join #ops-command-center and verify notification filters.
- Confirm pager ownership and escalation policy (who to call at night).
- Open UCC Confluence index and ensure playbook links open.
- Validate one synthetic alert fires and that you see full trace in Splunk/Tracing UI.
- Confirm access to model control plane (read-only) and to the gateway dashboards.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: UCC becomes a bottleneck or decision silo. Mitigation: timebox UCC authority; require re-handoff to service owner within 60 minutes unless continuing critical operations.
- Risk: alert fatigue from low-signal rules. Mitigation: early FPR tuning; add cooldowns and group alerts by incident ID.
- Risk: unclear customer comms. Mitigation: pre-approved message templates and CS liaison in every activation.

Open questions (notes-to-self for sync):
- What exact threshold should trigger automatic model fallback? (Ravi to propose by Week 1)
- Can we enrich alerts with the last-change commit id automatically? (Platform to prototype)
- Do we need a dedicated UCC phone bridge or is Slack Huddle + Zoom enough? (Ops to decide)

Immediate next actions (this week):
- [ ] Create JIRA epic: UCC-pilot-2026 (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Schedule 60-min tabletop for Jan 22 with serving-runtime + platform + product-hosted-api (owner: Ben)
- [ ] Provision Slack channel and add notification routing (owner: Ben)
- [ ] Draft the 4 playbook templates in Confluence (owner: Evan)
- [ ] Add model-fallback metric to serving runtime (owner: Ravi)

Appendix: Quick links and templates (placeholders)
- Playbook template: 1) Trigger 2) First action 3) Who to notify 4) Escalation ladder 5) Rollback criteria 6) Postmortem stub.
- Suggested shift cadence: 8am–4pm PT, 4pm–midnight PT, midnight–8am PT (optional for pilot). Rotate weekly.

Notes: The doc is intentionally operational and iterative. Keep edits here as the canonical UCC activation slate during the pilot. After the pilot, we will convert validated playbooks into the SLO lifecycle library (product + platform) and bake any pre-authorized mitigations into the rollout policies.

Slack links, ticket numbers, and Confluence IDs in this doc are placeholders — replace with final artifacts after Jan 22 tabletop.

-- Aisha (UCC pilot lead)
